title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured the effect of template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus limited automated repair) on deterministic-validator acceptance of LLM-generated network configurations under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We executed the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; complete_pairs_included=141) with a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). We incorporate reviewer-required clarifications: (1) runtime sampling configuration (execution/model_configuration.json: SHA-256 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd) shows "temperature": null (unset)—null does not imply deterministic sampling and provider defaults may apply; (2) provider-call audit counts (shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6; hosted_model_call_event_count = 156; completed = 147; failed = 9) establish that Guarded reused the shared_initial_candidate for paired comparisons and invoked extra model calls only when repair triggered (6 repair calls); (3) the preregistered benign-control (M=50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed and therefore no false-positive-blocking claims are made. We report the observed precision: paired difference = 0.04255 with 95% CI half-width ≈ 0.0319, which excludes zero. Limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, missing benign-control) restrict external claims. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support all numeric claims.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device CLI, promising reduced manual effort but risking syntax, topology, and semantic errors and exposure to prompt-injection vectors. Prior work shows that pairing generation with deterministic verification and repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[3]. This paper asks: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating at preventing adversarially crafted intents from producing unsafe or policy-violating configurations in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline? We contribute: (1) a preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) with a formal paired estimand measuring deterministic-validator acceptance-for-deployment; (2) artifact-backed analysis showing a small, statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations when using sanitization + verifier-gating + limited repair compared to an unguarded baseline on synthetic adversarial intents; (3) explicit reconciliations and clarifications requested by review (runtime sampling semantics, provider-call accounting, and an executed/unexecuted analysis inventory).
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide fast checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generate–validate pipelines [2],[37]. Recent NetOps experiments show LLMs produce useful draft configurations but commit syntax/semantic errors; integrating verifier feedback and automated repair improves outcomes in prototype tasks [3],[44]. Surveys and domain reviews emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally grounded metrics beyond textual matches [4],[5]. Security studies document prompt-injection and indirect-prompt vulnerabilities motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [6]. Tool-augmented LM orchestration (e.g., Toolformer) supports calling external checks during generation and repair [7]. Our study situates within these lines and provides a preregistered, artifact-backed confirmatory evaluation of sanitization + deterministic gating in a constrained synthetic adversary setting.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373) preregistered the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where each intent's binary outcome = 1 iff the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment. Because the preregistration included a natural-language H1 that referenced "unsafe/attack acceptance," we explicitly report results only against the archived formal estimand (validator-accepted = success). Design and interventions. Confirmatory paired design on N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Conditions: Baseline = single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini); Guarded = template-based input sanitization applied to the intent before generation and deterministic verifier-gating applied afterwards; the preregistered pipeline allowed at most one automated repair call per run. Generation semantics were implemented as shared_initial_candidate: the same initial generated candidate was recorded for both conditions where the shared stage applied; only deterministic validation, sanitization, or the permitted repair stage could create paired differences. Execution and instrumentation. Declared components (archived): generator = gpt-5-mini; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model configuration shows declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and "temperature": null in execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Null indicates the sampling temperature was unset in the archived configuration file; this does not guarantee deterministic (temperature=0) sampling because provider-side defaults may apply. Provider-call accounting from the archived deterministic reconciliation confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 6, and condition_counts: shared = 150, guarded = 6. These counts show Guarded reused the shared_initial_candidate in paired comparisons and invoked separate model calls only when repair was triggered (6 repair-stage calls). Missingness and exclusions. Pairs were excluded only when both paired runs were technical failures per the preregistered missingness_plan. The archived reconciliation (analysis artifacts) documents completed episodes = 282 and failed = 18; complete pairs included in primary analysis = 141. The preregistered benign-control (M=50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; this omission is treated as an unperformed preregistered item and is reported below in Results and Threats to Validity.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156. Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Observed outcomes on these 141 pairs: baseline_successes = 135 (135/141 = 0.9574468085); guarded_successes = 141 (141/141 = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Statistical inference. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Precision and post-hoc sensitivity. With complete_pairs = 141 the observed paired difference = 0.04255 and the 95% CI half-width ≈ 0.0319, so the estimated effect is small but the interval excludes zero at α=0.05 under the preregistered inference. Planned N was 150 (94% of the executed paired N = 141); the reduction in included pairs modestly reduces planned precision but did not prevent detecting the observed difference because the discordant count (n10 = 6) produced the exact p = 0.03125 and a CI excluding zero. Mechanism for discordant pairs. Archived validator and repair traces show the six discordant n10 pairs correspond to cases where sanitizer and/or the permitted automated repair changed the candidate or its presentation to the validator and thereby enabled acceptance where the unguarded baseline lacked correction. Because generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate, these paired differences arise from post-generation sanitization/repair and the validator gate rather than from differing initial first-pass sampling. Missingness sensitivity. Treating both-missing pairs (9 pairs where both runs failed) conservatively as failures yields baseline_successes = 135 and guarded_successes = 141 over N = 150 intents (baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000; guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400); the discordant counts driving McNemar remain unchanged and p = 0.03125. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore we do not report an empirical false-positive-blocking rate and caution that claims about blocking behavior on benign inputs cannot be made from this run.
sections.discussion: Interpretation relative to formal estimand. Because the binary outcome equals deterministic-validator acceptance-for-deployment, the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations on the included pairs (absolute increase ≈ 4.255 percentage points). The archived traces show that this improvement derived from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in six discordant cases rather than from gating rejecting otherwise accepted unsafe outputs. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting: (1) template-based sanitization together with limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (2) deterministic gating remains necessary to block invalid outputs, but gating policies should be co-designed with repair/sanitization to avoid rejecting reparable candidates. Threats to validity. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and does not capture full protocol runtime semantics. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization to multi-vendor, protocol-diverse production networks. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; exclusions were applied per the preregistered missingness_plan. Security coverage: adversary model was limited to mutations of synthetic intents; richer prompt-injection vectors in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines remain untested. Missing preregistered analyses: the unexecuted benign-control prevents reporting false-positive-blocking rates; we therefore do not claim reduced false-positive blocking in benign contexts. Recommendations. Practitioners should pair generators with deterministic validators and tested repair routines, expand validator coverage toward protocol-level semantics, explicitly record sampling settings, and run benign-control analyses before deploying gating/repair policies in production.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered confirmatory experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank shows that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated network configurations (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]) under the preregistered formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment). The observed improvement arose from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in six discordant cases; it should not be read as a direct measurement of reduced attacker-success without a distinct estimand that defines attacker-success as the outcome. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external claims. Future work must broaden validators, diversify models and vendors, run the preregistered benign-control and false-positive analyses, and evaluate defenses against richer prompt-injection threat models. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support the numeric claims reported here.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.

A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; we report and interpret results with respect to the archived formal estimand and explicitly disclose the phrasing ambiguity.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
